problem: The zero-crossing-rate formula uses sgn(x[n]) without ever defining it, so a student meeting it first here has to guess that sgn is the sign function (+1, 0 or −1). The sum limits are also left out, and it is not said that the average is over the N−1 neighbouring sample pairs inside the frame.
fix: Add: sgn(v) = +1 if v > 0, −1 if v < 0, 0 if v = 0; the sum runs over n = 1 to N−1, so there are N−1 adjacent pairs in the frame; |sgn(x[n]) − sgn(x[n−1])|/2 equals 1 when the waveform crosses zero between the two samples and 0 otherwise.

problem: The text says the stack of magnitudes |Xm[k]| 'is the short-time Fourier transform'. The STFT itself is complex-valued (it keeps phase); the magnitude, usually squared, is the spectrogram. The wording blurs a distinction examiners test.
fix: Say: the STFT is the complex sequence Xm[k] over frames m; the spectrogram displays |Xm[k]|, or often |Xm[k]|², so phase is thrown away in the picture.

problem: R(τ) is maximised at τ = 0 and falls off as τ grows simply because fewer samples overlap and the window tapers the frame ends. Taking the plain argmax over the whole allowed range can therefore return a multiple of the true pitch period (2T, 3T), and the 'largest value' rule is biased towards short lags.
fix: State the practical rule: skip τ = 0, search only τ between fs/F0max and fs/F0min, and pick the first strong peak (or use the normalised autocorrelation, dividing by the frame energy so the taper bias is removed).
